Nepal President Ram Chandra Paudel on Saturday expressed his "deepest" gratitude to India for its assistance to the flood-hit Himalayan nation during the difficult time.President Paudel thanked his counterpart in New Delhi, President Droupadi Murmu, and posted on X: "On behalf of the Government and the people of Nepal, I extend our deepest gratitude to Your Excellency Smt Droupadi Murmu for your kind concern and also for the generous support and solidarity extended by your government following the recent calamity in Nepal. Article Title: 'Took off for Kathmandu blissfully unaware': Shashi Tharoor on deadly Nepal floods
Article Text:
Tharoor said he was “blissfully unaware” of the devastation caused by a sudden flash flood in Nepal

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Thursday said that he was “blissfully unaware” of the devastation caused by a sudden flash flood in Nepal’s Rasuwa district when he left for Kathmandu on Wednesday."A severe, sudden flash flood struck northern Nepal’s Rasuwa district near the Tibet border, causing widespread destruction along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers. Global warming and/or an earthquake in Tibet may have caused a large chunk of a glacier to break off and fall into the valley below, experts surmise," Tharoor said in a post on X.Tharoor added that the flooding had destroyed at least 19 motorable bridges and washed away around 40 km of the Betrawati–Rasuwagadhi highway. Eight operational hydropower projects were also reported to have sustained heavy damage.Tharoor said he supported the Indian government’s immediate pledge of relief assistance to Nepal, adding that the country would need substantial help in responding to the destruction.He also expressed concern over the loss of life and those still missing, including Indians affected by the disaster."I fully support the Indian government’s immediate pledge of relief assistance.Nepal needs all the help it can get. My heart goes out to the victims and their loved ones, who include large numbers of Indian tourists, including a hundred performing the Kailash-Mansarovar Yatra. Prayers for the missing; may they be rescued soon," Tharoor said.The disaster has left at least 270 people dead and 826 missing in Nepal, while three people have died and 558 remain unaccounted for in Tibet, according to authorities.The scale of destruction has hampered rescue operations, with Nepalese officials reporting that dozens of bridges were destroyed and nearly 40 kilometres (25 miles) of roads damaged.The Nepalese Army launched helicopter operations on Thursday morning, rescuing more than 100 people from flood-affected areas, army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet said. At least eight foreign nationals were also airlifted to Kathmandu, while army teams evacuated people trapped inside facilities associated with the Trishuli hydropower project.India is also coordinating efforts to assist its nationals stranded in the affected areas. Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said five major groups, comprising around 288 Indian nationals, had been identified.“ The first group of 73 people who are working on the Trishuli-1 power project. Then, two separate groups of 37 and 49 nationals from Tamil Nadu, who traveled for Kailash Mansarovar Yatra through Samrat and Fly Everest Travels. There is a group of 32 Indian nationals from West Bengal who traveled with the help of Samrat Travels in Timure, which is in Rasuwa district.”“Then, a group of 61 Indian nationals from different states and then a group of 33 Indian nationals from Kerala. These are five major groups who comprise, by and large, 288 people that we are talking about,” he added.Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke with Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah and offered India’s assistance for rescue and relief operations.“India is prepared to provide Nepal with all possible types of humanitarian assistance,” PM Modi said, adding that Indian teams were coordinating rescue and relief efforts.The United Nations is also supporting the response, with agencies deploying personnel to assist local authorities. UN spokesperson Stephane Dujarric warned of a “massive humanitarian need” as rescue and relief operations continued.The disaster has also renewed concerns over the Himalayan region’s exposure to extreme weather events and glacial hazards, particularly in areas where difficult terrain and damaged infrastructure can complicate emergency response.
Article Summary: Tharoor said he was “blissfully unaware” of the devastation caused by a sudden flash flood in nepal on wednesday. The disaster has left at least 270 people dead and 826 missing in nepal, while three people have died and 558 remain unaccounted for in tibet.

Water rose 30 feet and at least 160 people were killed, while hundreds of others, including scores of Kailash Mansar-ovar pilgrims from India, remained missing after a flash flood and mudslide of unprecedented scale in Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers tore through a part of Nepal-Tibet border on Wednesday morning. It swept away settlements, hydropower units and the pilgrim route.Nepal Police put the toll at 157, while Chinese authorities reported three deaths and 265 people missing in Tibet’s Gyirong county. Nepal Police said 579 others — 466 foreigners from 28 countries and 113 Nepalis — remained untraced, including at least 133 Indians. Among the missing were at least 37 NRIs. Frighteningly, as many as 33 bodies were found 150km downstream at Chitwan, showing how far the dea-dly waters carried victims.Among the missing foreigners were 54 Americans, 34 Australians, 33 Britons, 24 Canadians, 19 Malaysians and 8 Koreans.Many were Kailash Mansarovar pilgrims, with nearly 400 of them, including the Indians, preparing to cross the Nepal-Tibet border or travelling through the region when the flood struck.Rescue personnel battled poor weather, mud, washed-out roads and high river levels even as authorities moved families from vulnerable settlements to safer locations.Nepal foreign minister Shisir Khanal told parliament that 29 police personnel and 44 soldiers remained untraced after floodwaters swept away their barracks in Rasuwa, while customs officials, hydropower workers and other employees stationed near the border were also missing. At the 20MW Langtang Khola Hydropower Project, dozens of workers are out of contact. The torrent also swept away or inundated security posts, customs facilities, banks and other establishments along the river corridor. Nepal PM Shah appealed for patience and unity as the Nepali Army, Nepal Police and Armed Police Force deployed helicopters, drones, boats and ground teams for search-and-rescue operations.Across the border, floods and mudslides severed several roads, communications and electricity around the (dry) Gyirong port, a key Nepal-Tibet crossing used by Kailash-Mansarovar pilgrims. Chinese president Xi Jinping called for “all-out efforts to search and rescue people who are missing”.The flood destroyed critical infrastructure across northern and central Nepal, with preliminary govt estimates showing at least 19 bridges and around 40 km of roads damaged or washed away; 13 hydropower projects were hit, and around 200 trucks were lost. The Nepal govt declared the worst-affected areas disaster-hit zones for the next 3 months and ordered authorities to provide free treatment to the injured.
Article Summary: Many were kailash mansarovar pilgrims, with nearly 400 of them, including the indians, preparing to cross the nepal-tibet border or travelling through the region when the flood struck. The flood destroyed critical infrastructure across northern and central nepal, with preliminary govt estimates showing at least 19 bridges and around 40 km of roads damaged or washed away.

Article Title: Pakistani drone detected in Jammu and Kashmir's Poonch, security forces put LoC sector on high alert
Article Text:

Drone tracked towards Mangalnar-Dabrote axis

Turkish military flights raise concerns

Security forces along the Line of Control (LoC) in Jammu and Kashmir have been put on high alert after fresh aerial activity originating from across the border was detected in the Poonch district.According to inputs from Army sources cited by news agency ANI, an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) from Pakistan was detected at around 8:05 pm on Friday.The drone was spotted hovering over the general area of Behrooti village in the Balakote area of Poonch's Mendhar sector, which falls under the operational area of responsibility of the 22 Jammu and Kashmir Rifles (22 JAK RIF).Military personnel tracked the UAV as it manoeuvred towards the Mangalnar-Dabrote side near the border before returning to Pakistan.Alert troops immediately logged the intrusion, following which the entire forward sector was placed under tight aerial and ground surveillance.Security forces launched the search operation at first light on Saturday in adjoining forward areas to check for any possible dropping of contraband or arms.Monitoring along the border remains active, and further official updates are awaited.The latest incident comes amid heightened security concerns along the India-Pakistan border and follows other suspected drone sightings reported in Jammu and Kashmir in recent weeks.Earlier this month, security forces launched a search operation after a suspected Pakistani drone was spotted over forward villages along the International Border in Jammu and Kashmir's Kathua district.The BSF and Jammu and Kashmir Police conducted searches to ensure that no weapons, explosives or other material had been dropped.A suspected Pakistani drone was also spotted in Rajouri's Sunderbani sector last month, after which security forces carried out a search operation but found nothing suspicious.Earlier in June, Army personnel opened fire after spotting a Pakistani drone over forward posts in the Balakote sector of Poonch, forcing it to retreat towards Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.Notably, the latest incident also comes days after an unusual increase in Turkish military transport flights to Pakistan raised concerns in Indian defence circles.Open-source flight trackers recorded a surge in Turkish C-130 Hercules and A400M aircraft flights between August 19 and 21, with the planes landing at Pakistani air bases, including Nur Khan, Masroor and Murid.There was speculation in defence circles that the flights may have carried military hardware, including unmanned aerial systems and air-defence equipment, although neither Pakistan nor Turkey officially confirmed the nature or cargo of the operations.Separately, security forces are carrying out massive search operations in the forested districts of Udhampur, Kathua and Rajouri following information about suspicious movement, according to news agency PTI.In Rajouri, another search operation was launched in Gaibas, Mithiyani, Mogla and Narla after villagers reported the movement of two suspected armed persons, believed to be terrorists.No contact with any suspected persons had been established so far, officials said.The latest incident in Poonch comes as security forces continue to maintain heightened surveillance along forward areas of Jammu and Kashmir.
Article Summary: Drone spotted hovering over behrooti village in balakote area of poonch's mendhar sector. Military personnel tracked the uav as it manoeuvred towards the mangalnar-dabrote side near the border before returning to pakistan. Comes amid heightened security concerns along the india-pakistan border.

Article Title: Nepal floods: Kathmandu agrees to foreign rescue help after pressure; India acts on its 'request'
Article Text:
Rescue teams search for survivors in flood-hit areas of Nepal as authorities seek international assistance

Why Nepal agreed

India dispatches 3rd consignment of aid

Nepal has agreed to accept foreign assistance for rescue operations after initially refusing the same as the scale of devastation from the floods continued to overwhelm relief efforts, The Kathmandu Post reported on Friday. India moved quickly to respond to Kathmandu's request for specialised support.MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said India was preparing to send a tunnel rescue team, with a reconnaissance team being flown in first to assess the situation and identify the equipment needed. India is also sending a medical team and has offered Bailey bridges along with technical teams to restore connectivity in affected areas."As requested by Nepal, we are preparing to send a tunnel rescue team, for which a recce team is being flown in first to assess the on-ground situation and what sort of equipment will be required. We are also sending a medical team to Nepal. In addition, we have also offered Bailey bridges along with associated technical teams so that connectivity can be restored quickly in the affected parts of Nepal and we can help in rescue and relief efforts. .. One Bailey bridge is already in Nepal and can be deployed for relief and connectivity efforts,” the MEA spokesperson Jaiswal said.Nepal reversed its earlier decision amid mounting pressure from countries whose nationals remain missing in the flood-hit areas.Several governments had urged Kathmandu to allow their specialist search-and-rescue teams to assist in locating survivors.“We received massive pressure from the international community to allow at least search-and-rescue teams and some experts because their citizens have also gone missing in the floods. We are allowing a limited number of experts in certain areas,” The Kathmandu Post reported quoting a senior government official.The decision also came as rescue operations made limited progress, with dozens of people still unaccounted for inside hydropower tunnels in Rasuwa and Nuwakot. The scale of the disaster has further increased the need for specialised tunnel-rescue expertise.Nepal also has limited capacity for DNA testing and forensic identification of bodies. Foreign experts will therefore assist with identifying the dead and ensuring that remains can be handed over to families as quickly as possible.India also dispatched its third consignment of humanitarian assistance to Nepal. The 10-tonne shipment included portable generators, dignity kits, food packets and water purification tablets, while an 11-member team of doctors, paramedics and tunnel-rescue specialists travelled on the same flight.The latest consignment takes India's total relief assistance to Nepal to 57.5 tonnes since August 26. The earlier shipments included temporary shelters, blankets, hygiene kits, solar lamps, medicines, dewatering pumps, generators, kitchen sets and food supplies.India has also offered Bailey bridges to help restore connectivity, with Jaiswal noting that one such bridge is already in Nepal and can be deployed for relief operations.
Article Summary: Nepal has agreed to accept foreign assistance for rescue operations after initially refusing the same. India moved quickly to respond to kathmandu's request for specialised support. India is preparing to send a tunnel rescue team, with a reconnaissance team being flown in first to assess the situation and identify the equipment needed.

Article Title: Sonia memoir row deepens, Congress alleges government pressure
Article Text:
Controversy erupts as Penguin Random House India reportedly pulls out of Sonia Gandhi memoir deal, Congress calls it "murder of democracy."

NEW DELHI: A controversy has erupted over the Indian publication of Sonia Gandhi's memoir 'Belonging', with Penguin Random House India (PRHI) reportedly pulling out of the deal following differences with the former Congress president over certain suggested edits.Calling it a "murder of democracy", Congress functionary Ashok Gehlot alleged that "pressure was put on Penguin India to remove the portions related to Narendra Modi , RSS and China's occupation of Indian territory during Modi's rule".Penguin, for its part, issued a carefully worded statement saying: "PRHI is not the publisher of 'Belonging' in India. Any suggestion that PRHI decided not to publish it because the author declined editorial changes does not accurately reflect the circumstances." The publishing house, however, defended its "prerogative and responsibility" to fact-check manuscripts and make recommendations to authors. It also said it remained "willing and keen" to publish the book. Earlier this year, PRHI stopped the distribution of cartoonist Joe Sacco's 'The Once and Future Riot', on the Muzaffarnagar riots.Interestingly, the US publisher of the memoir, Alfred A Knopf, is also a division of Penguin Random House.The international launch of ‘Belonging: A Journey in Love’, featuring a photo of a young Sonia on its cover, is scheduled for Nov 10. There is a question mark over who the Indian rights of ‘Belonging’ belong to, but the buzz is that HarperCollins may bag them.Gehlot also questioned why PRHI wanted changes to the Indian edition if Knopf was ready to publish the book worldwide in its original form. “What is the reason or what pressure is there that what is being published across the world cannot be published in India?” he asked. “Why is this truth being hidden from the people of India? Will the Modi govt alter even the facts by pressuring publishers?” he added.Gehlot said the integrity and dignity with which Sonia had served the country were exemplary. “Suppressing the book of a person of such stature, a senior leader of the nation, and former leader of the opposition, is tantamount to the murder of freedom of expression,” he said.Deputy leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha Gaurav Gogoi said, “No doubt there are those in the BJP govt who have now become afraid of a book being read by the people of India.”Congress, from its official social media handle to frontal organisations such as Seva Dal, lashed out at what it called the BJP’s attempt to sabotage the book of a senior national figure.
Article Summary: Controversy erupts as penguin random house india reportedly pulls out of sonia gandhi memoir deal, congress calls it "murder of democracy" the publishing house defended its "prerogative and responsibility" to fact-check manuscripts and make recommendations to authors.

Article Title: Second excavation phase at Kashmir Buddhist site starts today
Article Text:
Excavations for the second phase of the 2,000-year-old Buddhist site at Zehanpora in Baramulla to begin on Saturday

ZEHANPORA (BARAMULLA): Excavations will begin Saturday on the second phase of Zehanpora, a Buddhist site in north Kashmir’s Baramulla. J&K chief secretary Atal Dullo will inaugurate the project.The presence of a 2,000-year-old Buddhist civilisation at the site was discovered last year by Mohamad Ajmal Shah, a professor at University of Kashmir. It gained prominence after PM Narendra Modi mentioned it during his monthly radio programme Mann Ki Baat on Dec 28 last year.The Prime Minister recalled that people had noticed tall mounds in Zehanpora for years without knowing about their significance. What were first believed to be unusual rock formations were later found to resemble three Buddha stupas seen in photos in a French museum.According to Modi, the blurred photos, thousands of kilometres away, proved crucial as it showed three Buddhist stupas, helping archaeologists connect the dots and reconstruct Kashmir’s ancient past. The discovery reaffirms J&K’s rich cultural legacy.It all began in Oct 2023 when Shah was on a fellowship in France and came across the 100-odd old photos at Guimet Museum showing stupa domes in Baramulla. “I immediately realised I had visited the site.What struck me was the domes in the photos looked much larger than what we see now,” said Shah, attached to the varsity’s department of Central Asian Studies.Later, Shah requested J&K govt’s department of archaeology to fund the project and it agreed. Shah and his team started digging in Nov last year, initially discovering a hall identified as an apsidal (semi-circular) stupa.Shah and his team also found iron/copper artefacts, needles, decorated objects and other materials. “We identified wall alignments through drone images and excavated precisely at those points. There is a strong possibility that many structures and artefacts still lie preserved beneath the ground,” Shah said.Shah highlighted the possibility that the site was linked to the Fourth Buddhist Council (1st century CE). “Kashmir was a major centre of Buddhism in ancient times. It was here that Hinayana Buddhism evolved into Mahayana Buddhism, giving the religion a new philosophical and cultural form,” he said.Shah pointed out that the Chinese explorer Hiuen Tsang had mentioned Baramulla in his travel accounts. According to Shah, Tsang spent a night at Uskur, a Buddhist site near Baramulla town and visited several monasteries in the area. “This suggests Tsang must have visited the monastery at Zehanpora as well,” Shah said.
Article Summary: Excavations will begin saturday on the second phase of zehanpora, a buddhist site in north kashmir’s baramulla. The presence of a 2,000-year-old buddhist civilisation at the site was discovered last year by mohamad ajmal shah. It gained prominence after pm narendra modi mentioned it during his monthly radio programme mann ki baat.

That consciousness is Krishna Consciousness - we are one and we have been having it through these dualities of this world with the strong understanding that though there are so many diversities, dualities, conflicts, really it is all Krishna,” Bhagwat said.Anuttama Dasa, minister of communications and governing body commissioner of Iskcon, also welcomed Bhagwat's visit.“Mohan Bhagwat visited us and we are very grateful that he was here. Article Title: Have you done the truth test?
Article Text:
Thiruvalluvar captures the essence of this discipline in Kural 423:Epporul yaaryaarvaai ketpinum ApporulMeipporul kaanbadhu arivu.“Wisdom is to discover the truth in whatever is heard, irrespective of who says it.”Valluvar does not ask us to accept or reject an idea based on the identity of the speaker. He asks us to examine the truth within the statement.Iago’s words were believed because of who he appeared to be. Valluvar asks us to reverse that instinct: not “Who said this?” but “Is this true?”Truth is not measured by who speaks, but by what withstands examination.

Someone tells you that your closest friend has been speaking against you. At work, you hear that a colleague has spoiled your chances of a promotion. What do you do? Do you believe the person who told you, simply because you consider that person honest and dependable? Or do you pause and ask: How do I know if this is true?Shakespeare gave us a tragic answer to this question in ‘Othello’. Iago manipulates Othello by describing how his wife Desdemona’s handkerchief was with his friend Cassio, driving Othello into a jealous rage. The tragedy was not merely that Iago lied. It was that Othello failed to examine. He ended up killing Desdemona.How, then, does one ascertain truth? Is there a method by which we can distinguish what is real from what is merely reported, assumed or imagined?Interestingly, our ancestors believed in measuring everything accurately. Whether it was a piece of cloth or the jaggery needed for a pot of payasam, things had to be measured. In Tamil, there is a term, ‘Alavai iyal’ — the science of measurement. But measurement was not confined to physical objects. Indian philosophy also explored ways of measuring truth itself.These methods are called ‘pramanams’, means by which valid knowledge about what is true is obtained. Traditionally, six pramanams are described.The first is ‘pratyaksha’, or ‘kaatchi alavai’ — knowledge through direct perception using any of the senses. I smell gas and conclude there is a leak.The second is ‘anumana’, or ‘karuthal alavai’ — inference. I see smoke rising from a distance and infer that there must be a fire.The third is ‘agama pramanam’ or ‘urai alavai’ — knowledge obtained through texts.The fourth is ‘upamana pramanam’ or ‘uvamai alavai’ — knowledge through comparison. Understanding the unknown through knowledge about the known.The fifth is ‘arthapatti’ or ‘porul alavai’ — postulation from circumstances. The house is unusually quiet. We may infer that there was a big fight and now everybody is silent. It is not direct knowledge, but a conclusion drawn from circumstances.The sixth is ‘anupalabdhi’ or ‘inmai alavai’, knowledge through non-perception or absence. If someone claims to have seen a polar bear in Antarctica, the claim can be rejected because polar bears are native to the Arctic.These are not merely philosophical categories, but disciplines for the journey towards truth. Without them, our minds can easily become prisoners of assumptions and biases.Bias is perhaps our first obstacle. If someone we admire says something, we are inclined to accept it. If someone we dislike says the same thing, we may instinctively reject it. In both cases, we judge the statement by the person rather than examining its truth.The pramanas provide a framework to go beyond what our eyes can see without letting imagination outrun reason. They help us test assumptions, examine evidence and separate fact from illusion.
Article Summary: Thiruvalluvar captures the essence of this discipline in kural 423:epporul yaaryaarvaai ketpinum apporulmeipporul kaanbadhu arivu. Truth is not measured by who speaks, but by what withstands examination.

Article Title: 61% of children in India exposed to one more month of heat stress due to climate change: Study
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: In India, 61 per cent of children, or 145 million, are exposed to at least one additional month of heat stress due to climate change every year, new global research has estimated.Findings published in the journal Science Advances show that climate change has doubled the number of children aged up to nine exposed to at least five total months of dangerous heat stress per year -- from 59 million to 118 million (50 per cent of children).An international team of researchers, led by those at Vrije Universiteit Brussel in Belgium, said the study is the first-ever analysis quantifying how heat exposure directly linked to climate change affects different age groups globally, both now and in the near future.Excess heat disrupts the human body's normal functioning, aggravates underlying diseases, and can lead to serious complications such as heatstroke, dehydration, and organ failure.The study focuses on humid heat, which is more dangerous than dry heat because it impedes the body's ability to sweat to cool back down, leading to dangerous levels of heat stress.Globally, up to 560 million children aged 0-9 -- 43 per cent of all children in this age group -- are living through at least one additional month of heat stress per year due to human-induced climate change, the analysis found.The exposure outpaces that for any other age group and is nearly triple the 190 million people (30 per cent) aged 60-69 experiencing the additional health threat, the researchers said.They added climate change is increasing humid heat the most in tropical regions and poorer countries, where populations are younger, and more children are therefore affected.South Asia, Southeast Asia, and West Africa are the regions with the highest number of children exposed to dangerous heat stress today, the team said."Climate change is already causing hundreds of millions of children to suffer from dangerous heat worldwide, posing severe risks to their health. Children in developing countries face (a) disproportionate exposure to climate extremes now and into the future, despite contributing the least to historical greenhouse gas emissions," lead author Rosa Pietroiusti, a PhD researcher at Vrije Universiteit Brussel, said."At the same time, poverty, inadequate housing, limited access to cooling, and overstretched health care systems leave many children with few ways to protect themselves from the heat," Pietroiusti said.The number of children affected by an additional month of dangerous heat is expected to increase to 620 million (49 per cent of all children) and 650 million (59 per cent) children under projected climate change scenarios of 1.5 degrees Celsius and 2 degrees Celsius of global warming, respectively.In India, 166 million children (74 per cent) are projected to experience at least one additional month of heat stress per year under a global warming of 1.5 degrees Celsius.The figure could be 169 million children (96 per cent) under a global warming of 2 degrees Celsius.
Article Summary: In india, 61 per cent of children, or 145 million, are exposed to at least one additional month of heat stress due to climate change every year. South asia, southeast asia, and west africa are the regions with the highest number of children exposed to dangerous heat stress today.

Article Title: India & China announce 8-point boundary consensus before Xi's visit, target early & substantial harvest in border delimitation
Article Text:
According to the joint statement, both sides agreed that any situation on the ground would be addressed promptly.

NEW DELHI: India and China jointly announced Wednesday that the Special Representatives (SR) dialogue on the boundary question - co-chaired by Ajit Doval and Wang Yi this week - had led to an 8-point consensus, signalling some positive progress in boundary talks ahead of President Xi Jinping's visit to India next month.These included advancing consultations for an "early and substantial harvest" of boundary delimitation, setting up more meeting points and hotlines to improve border management, improving understanding of LAC and addressing ground situation through diplomatic and military engagements, expanding trans-border trade and rivers cooperation. The consensus was announced in a rare joint statement after the SR talks.Building upon the outcomes from the last round of talks in 2024, the 2 sides agreed that the Expert Group on Boundary Delimitation and Working Group on Border Management would advance discussions on an “Early and Substantial Harvest” of boundary delimitation and Border Management. The first task for both these groups would be to agree on their respective Terms of Reference, said the joint statement.India and China had agreed last year to set up an expert group under the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on India-China Border Affairs (WMCC), to explore early harvest in boundary delimitation in the India-China border areas.The formulation was changed to early and substantial on this occasion.Two additional meeting points for military talks and 2 more channels of border military hotlines in the Eastern and Middle Sectors were agreed upon to reinforce border management measures, according to both sides.“The two sides underlined their commitment to advancing negotiations on a framework for the settlement of the boundary question in accordance with the Agreement on Political Parameters and Guiding Principles for Settlement of the India-China Boundary Question signed in 2005 and the consensus reached in subsequent SR Talks in pursuit of a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable solution,” said the MEA in a statement. Unlike the Chinese readout of the talks on Tuesday, the joint statement did not mention package settlement or solution, although the 2005 agreement talks about making adjustments to reach a package settlement.The two sides also reaffirmed their commitment to upholding the guidance received from Modi and Xi, maintaining peace and tranquility in the border areas and creating an atmosphere for healthy and steady development of bilateral relations.According to the joint statement, both sides agreed that any situation on the ground would be addressed promptly through existing diplomatic and military channels, including the WMCC, local commander‑level meetings and other agreed mechanisms, to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the LAC. “The two sides discussed ways to improve understanding of LAC in appropriate areas, for better border management,” said the joint statement.Both sides also noted the progress on trans-border cooperation, with the Indian side appreciating the efforts made by the Chinese side to increase the number of batches of Indian official pilgrimage Kailash-Manasarovar Yatra (KMY) in the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.“Both sides appreciated the reopening of the three designated border trading points. The two sides agreed to strengthen exchanges and cooperation in border trade, pilgrimage and other areas, with the view to work together to create an atmosphere featuring dialogue, peace, consultation and cooperation in the border areas,” said the joint statement.India and China also agreed to hold the next meeting of the India-China Expert-Level Mechanism on Trans-border Rivers in September and maintain communication on issues including hydrological data sharing, and renewal of the relevant MoUs. It’s important for India that China shares hydrological information during emergency situations based on humanitarian considerations. The two sides agreed to hold the 26th round of SR Talks in India in 2027.
Article Summary: India and china announced wednesday that the special representatives (sr) dialogue on the boundary question had led to an 8-point consensus. The consensus was announced in a rare joint statement after the sr talks. The two sides agreed to hold the 26th round of sr talks in india in 2027.
